name: Breifine
summary: The frontier hills over Marfach: four duns on Caimheul's old stones, Evern's ring, the war's dead and the keen that comes up through the floors.

facts.text: Monsters: spectral manslayers (50-53), umber bears, ghastly Midgard invaders, undead Briton invaders and skeletal dwarf invaders (43-46), bloodletters and earthshakers (48-49), grogans, empyrean guardians, torcan, a boogie man, a bananach, a moss monster, a Parthenon guard; Evern (76, Faerie Court) with a wraith drake (67) beside him; Morven (46, Fomorian), Raemon (45) and Witch Xia (28).
Bréifne was a medieval kingdom of north-west Ireland; the bánánach is a battle-spirit of Irish tradition that shrieks over the field.
Morven's Return: 'Slay Raemon, the third heir, at the cyclops tower'. Season of Remorse ends with Witch Xia and her summoned pet.
Evern: level 76, faction Faerie Court; the fairies that land on his stones keep him alive (Evern.cs).

Living Server lore: the duns on Caimheul's stones; the keen through the floors, loudest when a keep changes hands; the candle in the window when a Lady falls; the three realms' dead; Evern's ring older than the keeps; Nóra's account of the hills.
Tier C named spawn of Breifine: Witch Xia (28, a small orc body), alone; Season of Remorse asks for 'Witch Xia and her summoned pet', but no pet spawn stands near her in the world data.

story:
Breifine was the old families' country before it was the frontier. Its hills were the hill-chieftains', and the greatest of them, Caimheul, kept his dún on the highest ground over the caves where the families buried their dead. When the realm war came the realm built its keeps on the old stones, because they were there and they were good, and Dun Bolg, Dun Crimthain, Dun Da Behnn and Dun nGed stand now on the foundations of a chieftain whose household never stopped standing under them. The keen of Marfach comes up through the keeps' floors. The garrisons say it is loudest the night a keep changes hands.

Each dun has its chieftain, and each chieftain keeps a custom of the old families. Chieftain Bolg keeps the western dun and settles quarrels by single combat in the yard, the way the hill-chieftains did. Chieftess Crimthain keeps the eastern dun and keeps hostages' names on her wall, the names of the children of the frontier families she has sworn to protect, so that she never forgets whom she answers to. Chieftess Da Behnn keeps the southern dun and keeps the keeners' custom: when a Lady falls under the hill, a candle in her window. Dun nGed, the smallest, keeps no custom anyone can name, and its garrison likes it that way.

The war's dead walk the hills between. The ghastly Midgard invaders and undead Briton invaders and skeletal dwarves of the south are the enemy realms' fallen, who heard the keen from below and got up; the spectral manslayers in the north are older, and nobody agrees whose they were. A bananach, a battle-spirit of the old tales, shrieks over the northern field at night, and the bloodletters and earthshakers walk the high ground with it. The keeners of the Breifine hills sing the right keen when a hosting comes home short, so that the ones left on the field go on and do not join them.

In the middle of it stands Evern's ring. It is older than any keep and older than Caimheul's dún: a ring of stones around a fairy lord who has stood there since the Veil came down, kept alive by the fairies that land on his stones and are spent there, one by one. A wraith drake circles over him. The garrisons of all four duns leave him alone, and he leaves them alone, and the frontier's oldest saying is that Evern was here before the war and will be here after it.

Morven's house stands on the eastern edge of Breifine, the Fomorian lord's who held these hills before the keeps; he is there still, and his third heir, Raemon, keeps the cyclops tower in the west. Witch Xia keeps a hollow in the south, where the morsmutare witches' remorse comes to its end. And in the east, past Dun Crimthain, the way goes down under the hill into Marfach.

Why does it matter? Because Breifine is the frontier that remembers. The other hills were empty when the keeps went up; Breifine had a household under it, and the household is still there, and the war is fought on its roof.
legend: Breifine is frontier (RvR) between Cruachan Gorge and Emain Macha: four keeps, Dun Bolg (west), Dun Crimthain (east), Dun Da Behnn (south) and Dun nGed. The Marfach Caverns entrance is in the east past Dun Crimthain. PvE: realm-war dead (ghastly Midgard, undead Briton and skeletal dwarf invaders, 43-46) in the south, spectral manslayers (50-53) and bloodletters and earthshakers (48-49) in the north, umber bears, grogans. Evern (76) stands in his stone ring in the middle with a wraith drake (67) next to him: kill the fairies on his stones first or they keep him alive. Morven (46) and Raemon (45, at the cyclops tower) are Morven's Return; Witch Xia (28) ends Season of Remorse. Breifine custom: put a candle in the window when a Lady of Marfach falls, and say the right keen when a hosting comes home short.

loremaster.intro: Breifine, the frontier that remembers. Its four duns, [Bolg], [Crimthain], [Da Behnn] and [nGed], stand on [Caimheul]'s stones; the [keen] comes up through their floors; the war's [dead] walk the hills; [Evern]'s ring is older than all of it.

topics.Bolg: Dun Bolg, the western dun, where Chieftain Bolg settles quarrels by single combat in the yard, as the hill-chieftains did.
topics.Crimthain: Dun Crimthain, the eastern dun, where Chieftess Crimthain keeps the names of the frontier children she has sworn to protect on her wall. The Marfach way is beyond it.
topics.Da Behnn: Dun Da Behnn, the southern dun, where Chieftess Da Behnn keeps the keeners' custom: a candle in the window when a Lady falls under the hill.
topics.nGed: Dun nGed, the smallest dun, which keeps no custom anyone can name.
topics.Caimheul: The greatest of the hill-chieftains of Breifine, whose dún stood where the keeps stand now, over the caves of the dead. His household is still under the hill, in Marfach.
topics.keen: The keen of Marfach, which comes up through the keeps' floors and is loudest the night a keep changes hands. The Breifine keeners sing the right keen back when a hosting comes home short.
topics.dead: The enemy realms' fallen, Britons and Midgard men and dwarves, who heard the keen from below and got up; and the spectral manslayers of the north, older, whose nobody knows. A bananach shrieks over them.
topics.Evern: A fairy lord in a ring of stones in the middle of Breifine, older than the keeps, kept alive by the fairies that land on his stones. A wraith drake circles over him. He was here before the war.
topics.Witch Xia: Witch Xia keeps a hollow in the south of Breifine, alone, and the morsmutare witches' remorse comes to its end with her. She is no woman of the realm but one of the orc-folk who came with the invaders and stayed when they went home, small and old and clever, and the morsmutare witches learned their craft from her. The empyrean guardian of the stone ring sends the young to her last. The quest-givers speak of a pet she calls up. Nobody has seen it.

book.title: Under the Duns: Breifine, from Nóra of the Breifine hills
pages: I am a keener's daughter of the Breifine hills, and I have written of the caves already. This is the roof. The realm built its keeps on Caimheul's stones because the stones were good and the ground was high, and nobody asked the household under them. The household answers anyway. When a keep changes hands, the garrison hears the keen come up through the floor, louder than any other night, and the chieftains no longer pretend it is the wind. They have learned to sleep through it, mostly, the way a family sleeps through an old relative's snoring.

Each dun keeps one of the old families' customs, whether it knows it or not. Bolg settles quarrels in the yard, single combat, as the hill-chieftains did. Crimthain keeps the names of the children she protects on her wall, which is what the hostage-houses were before they went wrong. Da Behnn keeps a candle for my mother's trade, and lights it in the window when a Lady falls. Dun nGed keeps nothing, and I think that is a custom too: a keep that has chosen to forget, on a hill that never does.

The war's dead heard the keen. The Britons and the men of Midgard who fell in the south got up in their armour and walk there still, and the dwarves with them, and the frontier keeners will not sing for them, because they are not ours to send on. We sing for our own, when a hosting comes home short, the right keen, facing forward, so that the ones left on the field go on. Over the north field at night the battle-spirit shrieks, and we do not sing for her either.

In the middle of the hills is Evern's ring. My grandmother's grandmother said it was old when Caimheul was young. The fairy lord in it has stood there since the Veil came down, and the small fairies land on his stones and are spent there to keep him alive, one by one, and a wraith drake circles over him. The garrisons leave him be. He was here before the war, the frontier says, and he will be here after it. I believe it. Breifine keeps everything, the living and the dead and the old lord in his ring, and it gives back only what it is sung for.
